title: emfit.job.v1 — a job submitted to the emfit resource
description: The input document of the emfit resource contract. It is specified at decisions.md:7012-7093 (section 101.19, subsection (b)) and restated, with the readings behind every choice, in docs/design/job_schema.md. A job states what is to be solved: the geometry, the materials, the excitation ports, the observables wanted, the frequencies and the tolerance. What stays on the tool's side of the boundary — meshing, time stepping, iteration count, choice of solver — is not expressible here, by design (decisions.md:7016-7022). Units: every numeric member carries its unit in its name; the job is unit-suffixed, the tool's interior is SI, and the conversion happens at the boundary (emfit/demos.py:76, :77, :91). The one unit trap this schema cannot leave to the caller is the frequency, which is in GHz and not Hz; see the description of frequencies_ghz. The object is closed (additionalProperties false) so that a typo is refused at submit time; the tolerance obligation of decisions.md:7061-7063 — that a reader must ignore members it does not know — is carried by the reading side, not by this schema, and the asymmetry is recorded in docs/design/job_schema.md.

schema.description: The document's own name and version. It is a constant, not a hint: a document that says anything else is not an emfit.job.v1 and must be refused rather than reinterpreted (decisions.md:7059).

geometry.description: What is to be solved, as either a board file or a parametric shape. Exactly one of the two forms is accepted, discriminated by the kind member (decisions.md:7028, :7036-7038).

materials.description: The substrate the geometry is built on. Nothing else is stated here: conductor and boundary treatments are the tool's, per the boundary rule at decisions.md:7016-7022.

sources.description: The excitation ports, at least one. Order is not significant, and a port is named so that observables and provenance can refer to it by name rather than by position (decisions.md:7030).

observables.description: What the caller wants back, at least one, named in the same language the result uses for tolerance_achieved (decisions.md:7031, :7050). An observable this schema cannot name cannot be asked for; that is the version-bump rule, not an oversight.

frequencies_ghz.description: The frequencies at which the observables are wanted, at least one. The numbers are GIGAHERTZ, not hertz: the tool's interior is SI and this field is the boundary, where the conversion is a single multiplication by 1e9 (emfit/demos.py:91, f_target=float(f0_ghz) * 1e9). A caller who writes 2.4e9 here has written a valid number and a 2.4 EHz request, which no type keyword can catch — hence the normative ceiling of 1000.0 GHz (1 THz) below. The ceiling is a unit guard, not a physics claim: every fixture in this repository runs between 1 and 20 GHz (emfit/demos.py:392). A time-domain solver accumulates at these frequencies and echoes the set back in its provenance; a frequency-domain solver solves at them (docs/design/core_contract.md, section 2).

items.description: One frequency, in gigahertz. Must be positive and no greater than 1000.0 GHz.

tolerance.description: The accuracy the caller requires. The kind names the measure and the value is its magnitude in that measure's own units, so the pair is never ambiguous about what 1e-3 is 1e-3 of. Scope: as drafted at decisions.md:7032 the tolerance is one value for the whole job while the result's tolerance_achieved is keyed per observable; that asymmetry is a recorded defect (decisions.md:7087-7089) and this schema does not repair it — it reproduces the draft, and the repair is deferred to emfit.job.v2 rather than made silently here.

geometry_kicad.title: geometry, board-file form
geometry_kicad.description: A geometry read out of a KiCad board file, which is the form decisions.md:7028 shows and the only one it shows.

kind.description: Discriminator of the board-file form. It is the constant kicad, so that a reader knows which members to expect before reading them.

path.description: Path to a .kicad_pcb file, interpreted relative to the directory holding the job document unless it is absolute. The schema checks only that it is a non-empty string: existence, readability and stackup are the tool's business and a path check here would be a second, weaker truth (decisions.md:7016-7022). The board reader that would consume it already exists (emfit/cli.py, the board subcommand).

geometry_parametric.title: geometry, parametric form
geometry_parametric.description: A geometry stated as dimensions rather than as a file. Required by decisions.md:7036-7038, which records that every fixture in this repository is parametric and that a board-only schema could not express a single test that justifies it. The members are deliberately physical and not mesh-shaped: cell counts, time stepping and station placement stay solver-side (decisions.md:7016-7022).

kind.description: Discriminator of the parametric form. It is the constant parametric, and it is what a reader switches on.

box_length_mm.description: Total length of the computational box along the line direction, in millimetres, absorber included. This is the quantity the tree reports as geometry['length'] in metres (emfit/studies.py:3262); the job states it in millimetres because every human-facing length in the tree does (emfit/demos.py:389, :407-409).

strip_width_mm.description: Width of the conducting strip, in millimetres. The tree derives it as strip_cells * cell with cell = substrate_h_mm / substrate_cells (emfit/demos.py:76-77); the job states the width itself so that the mesh relation is not baked into the contract.

substrate_cells.description: How many cells the substrate slab is discretised into. It is dimensionless because it is a count, and it is here rather than solver-side because it is the one mesh parameter the realised cell size depends on, cell = substrate_h_mm / substrate_cells (emfit/demos.py:76-77).

materials.title: materials
materials.description: The substrate: permittivity and thickness, both required. An absent thickness would leave the cell size undefined for the parametric form, so neither is optional.

substrate_eps_r.description: Relative permittivity of the substrate slab, dimensionless and therefore unit-free. It must be at least 1.0: a value below vacuum would be a metamaterial claim the tool does not make, and the demo studies restrict themselves to 1.0-16.0 (emfit/demos.py:386).

substrate_h_mm.description: Thickness of the substrate slab, in millimetres, strictly positive. It is also the length that sets the cell size, cell = substrate_h_mm / substrate_cells, exactly as the demo does it (emfit/demos.py:76-77); the tool converts to metres at the boundary.

source.title: one excitation port
source.description: One port. A port is placed either by board net or by parametric position, and by exactly one of the two: the oneOf below requires that at least one of net and x_mm be present, and the design note records that the cross-document rule — net goes with kicad geometry, x_mm with parametric — is deliberately not enforced here, because JSON Schema cannot see the sibling geometry from inside this object without duplicating the whole document.

kind.description: The kind of source. Only modal_port is named: a modal port excites the mode the extraction layer computes, which is the only excitation the tree has a measurement path for (emfit/ports.py, the mode profile and DftAccumulator machinery).

name.description: Name of the port, unique within the job. It is the handle the result's provenance uses to say which port a tolerance was achieved on, so it must be a stable identifier rather than a label: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (decisions.md:7030).

net.description: Board net the port sits on, for the board-file geometry form. It must match a net the board reader reports; the schema cannot check that, and a name that matches nothing is a tool-side failure rather than a schema failure (decisions.md:7030).

x_mm.description: Position of the port plane along the line direction, in millimetres from the near wall of the box, for the parametric geometry form. This is the job-level spelling of the tree's ix_port * cell (emfit/studies.py:2566), which is a node count times a cell size and therefore not a contract quantity.

observable.title: one observable
observable.description: One quantity the caller wants back. Only scattering parameters are named, because only they have a Touchstone artefact to live in (decisions.md:7031, :7047-7053).

kind.description: The kind of observable. Only sparam is named; a field dump would be a different kind and would need a different result artefact, which is a version bump.

name.description: The S-parameter, in the form S<output><input> with two digits each, e.g. S11 or S21. The two-digit form is not decoration: it is what makes S1 and S21 distinguishable, and it is the key the result's tolerance_achieved uses, so a laxer pattern here would produce a result the caller cannot look up (decisions.md:7031, :7050).

tolerance.title: tolerance
tolerance.description: The accuracy required, as a kind/units pair. The kind fixes what the number measures so that the number alone is never ambiguous.

kind.description: The measure the tolerance is expressed in. sparam_abs means absolute magnitude on the complex S-parameter, the form decisions.md:7033 shows and the only one this version defines.

value.description: The magnitude of the tolerance, in the units the kind names: for sparam_abs it is an absolute difference in the complex S-parameter, dimensionless, and it must be strictly positive. It is the number the tool compares its own achieved error against before it may return status ok rather than degraded (decisions.md:7055-7057).
